answer: I'd like to describe a celebration that my whole family still talks about. A special occasion I celebrated with real joy was my parents' wedding anniversary, which my sisters and I organised as a surprise last year. We had been planning it secretly for weeks, which made the anticipation even more exciting, and keeping it from my mother was not easy, because she notices everything. My elder sister came from Dhaka with her husband and their two children, and my grandparents travelled in from the village. We decorated the house, invited close relatives and arranged all their favourite food, including the biryani my father loves. My younger sister was in charge of the cake, and I handled the guest list. The look of genuine surprise and delight on my parents' faces was absolutely [[priceless]]. It was a wonderfully [[heartwarming]] evening, full of laughter, old stories and a few happy tears. My grandmother even told us how my parents first met, which none of us had heard before. What made it so special was seeing the whole family come together to honour them. In our increasingly busy lives, these gatherings feel [[few and far between]], and so all the more precious. My four-year-old nephew kept trying to blow out the candles before anyone else, which had everyone in fits of laughter. I remember feeling an overwhelming sense of gratitude and love that evening. Honestly, occasions like this remind me of what truly matters. The whole event was thoroughly [[unforgettable]], and I think it meant just as much to us as it did to my parents. It is a night I will always [[treasure]].

followUps.q: Do you often celebrate special occasions with your family?
followUps.answer: Yes, especially Eid, when everyone tries to be together. We are a close-knit family, so even smaller occasions like birthdays usually end with a big dinner at home.

followUps.q: What did your parents say about the surprise?
followUps.answer: My father was lost for words, which is rare for him. My mother cried a little and then immediately started worrying whether there was enough food for everyone, which made us all laugh.

note: Added sisters, elder sister's family from Dhaka and grandparents from the village; plain marks 'rare' and 'memorable' replaced by 'few and far between', 'unforgettable', 'treasure'.
